series.name: Mom & Pop Papers
series.tagline: Short papers on the basic teachings of the Two-Kingdom Citizen. Read it more than once. Talk it through. Then try explaining it to someone without the sheet.
series.org: Champions Network · An initiative of the Lutheran Center for Religious Liberty

papers.title: Two Kingdoms — Church and State?
papers.kicker: The Founders weren't afraid of too much church. They were afraid of too much power.
body: When the Bible teaches that God engages the World for the sake of the world in two distinct ways, modern people tend to hear “separation of Church and State” – as if the Church needs to keep quiet in the public sphere of American culture. The Bible teaches no such thing, however, and the American Founding Fathers weren’t afraid of too much “church” in society. They were afraid of too much power being amassed in the state.

So, what’s the point? Well, when talking about “Church and State,” remember that both the Church and the State are public entities under God’s authority and direction. The “state,” however, doesn’t just include politics and law enforcement. Rather, it is the public ordering of the world for the sake of civility, temporal justice, and peace, and that also includes the vocations of Father and Mother (families), and even the value and purpose of work and enterprise. That means all the various ways in which people seek to serve those they love with honest enterprise and committed friendship are also part of the “state”. When these things are ordered well, the Bible says that “Believers strive for excellence in all they do to give God glory and to serve others in His Name.” Thus, a well-ordered state will seek not to silence the church and keep it out of the public sphere, but to set believers free to strive for excellence and to serve others for the good of the whole society.

body.quote: Of all the dispositions and habits which lead to political prosperity, religion and morality are indispensable supports.

body: The American Founding Fathers understood this well. Washington and the other Founders knew that a well-ordered society is impossible without a virtuous citizenry, and they knew that the church is indispensable for encouraging such public morality. In a well-ordered society, therefore, the state seeks to protect the church’s involvement in the public sphere so that it can contribute to the moral education of the citizens and, in turn, to the preservation of society.

The idea of “Separation of Church and State” wasn’t to keep these beneficial aspects of the church out of the public sphere, rather it was to prevent the concentration of too much power in one institution. The Founding Fathers didn’t want a society without a church, they wanted political and religious power to be separated into distinct institutions, church and state, which would mutually support each other in support of the public good.

The Two-Kingdom view of life, then, sees the wonderful value of a government working well within its boundaries, and the powerful potential of a church that is set free to proclaim the Gospel unrestrained. To that end, a Christian Two-Kingdom citizen, is “Set Free, to live freely for others in Christ.” They are ready to put their “Temporal liberties to work to proclaim and embody the eternal liberties of Christ,” just as the Apostle Paul put his Roman Citizenship to work for the Gospel in Acts 16.
questions: What is the danger of the left-hand kingdom amassing too much power over the right-hand kingdom?
What is the danger of the right-hand kingdom amassing too much power over the left-hand kingdom?
What does it mean to put your temporal liberties to work for the Gospel?

papers.title: Christian Engagement of the World — Dynamic Differentiation
papers.kicker: Get involved. And never lose sight of what is ultimate.
body: A Recipe for Christian involvement in the public sphere. First, be dynamically involved, engaging with the culture for the sake of the church and for the sake of the public good. Second, discern and differentiate between God’s two kingdoms. Recognize the temporal role of the government in preserving peace and security, and recognize the eternal role of the church in bringing the good news of salvation to the world. Neither the church nor the state ought to usurp the other’s role.

body.quote: Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s and give to God what is God’s.

body: In this dynamic differentiation, Jesus’ words in Luke 20:25 guide us. The two important questions for good “public” engagement of issues and policies are:

list: What does God desire of Caesar?
What does God want His people to do in support of Caesar?

body: Paul answered both questions in Romans 13:

body.scripture: Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God. Therefore whoever resists the authorities resists what God has appointed, and those who resist will incur judgment. For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Would you have no fear of the one who is in authority? Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval, for he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not bear the sword in vain. For he is the servant of God, an avenger who carries out God’s wrath on the wrongdoer. Therefore one must be in subjection, not only to avoid God’s wrath but also for the sake of conscience. For because of this you also pay taxes, for the authorities are ministers of God, attending to this very thing. Pay to all what is owed to them: taxes to whom taxes are owed, revenue to whom revenue is owed, respect to whom respect is owed, honor to whom honor is owed.

body: God desires Caesar (the government) to be his servant for good, to punish wrongdoers, to encourage those who do well, and to bear the sword for the preservation of society. Christian citizens, likewise, are called to give honor to this work of the government and to respect those in authority. Nevertheless, we also recognize that our leaders can’t solve the biggest problem of life – sin. Power and government can control bad folks to a degree with the sword, but the only thing that can change the heart is the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

When it comes to public life, therefore, we Christians need to be “dynamically engaged,” encouraging the government in its God given, left-hand kingdom role to preserve justice, safety, and civility. We also need to recognize, however, God’s more important right-hand kingdom work. In his left-hand kingdom, God blesses his people with temporal goods, curbing evil through law-enforcement, and providing for the blessings of society through marriage, vocation, and commerce. In his right hand kingdom, however, God brings to his people the eternal and ultimate gift of salvation through Christ. As two-kingdom citizens, Christians do all the temporal things of the left hand kingdom ultimately in service of the eternal things of the Gospel.

In Biblical times there were many different governing authorities. At the time of Jesus the Roman Empire dominated and Caesar ruled as king. In the United States, the Constitution makes the citizens sovereign, creating a government “of the people, by the people, for the people.” That remarkable turnaround has brought tremendous blessings of freedom to America, but with such freedom, it is even more important for Christians to be disciplined, religious citizens, and to use our freedom well. St. Paul’s admonition in Romans 13 cuts both ways. We aren’t just called to honor those elected officials, we too need to be honorable, and in America, we don’t just submit to the laws of the land, we also have the responsibility to participate in creating those laws for the good of all.

To that end we encourage Christians to be dynamic. Get involved in the public sphere, advocate for the God-given role of government, model the virtues of a good citizen and thus have no fear of a good government. All the while, however, realize what is ultimate and fundamental to promote the spreading of the gospel to all the world. Dynamic Differentiation. Get involved (dynamic) but always be active in appreciating God’s primary work – the salvation of sinners (differentiation).

This calls for Christians to be a unique kind of citizen no matter what country they are in, but in the United States, it gives us a wonderful way to exercise our free citizenship in Christian love and service toward others.
questions: To be dynamic means to be actively engaged. How is God dynamic in the left-hand kingdom?
To be dynamic means to be actively engaged. How is God dynamic in the right-hand kingdom?

The first line of the United States Constitution states that “We the people” are the ones that establish the laws. How does that impact our being involved in the enactment and enforcement of these laws?

papers.title: Christian Public Engagement — Reformation Restraint
papers.subtitle: A cautious approach to demanding societal outcomes
papers.kicker: God is at work in the world — even through people who don't believe in Him.
body: It seems there is so much to be angry about these days, and everyone thinks that they have the answers that will make it all better. We’ve all witnessed and can understand that widespread sentiment that we are just one more resolution, one more bill, or one more election away from getting everything right. Then we’ll be at peace. Then our problems will be solved. What does the two-kingdom, Christian citizen do?

When it comes to ideas for radically changing things “to get it right,” a Two-Kingdom citizen ought to be hesitant at first. Why? He or she knows that God is at work in the world through the left-hand Kingdom, even through people who aren’t believers in Him. Likewise, the outcomes God brings about are often very different from what we believe is the perfect future, and as Christians we ought to accept that fact with humility, recognizing that God’s ways are higher than ours. This is what we call Reformation Restraint - restraining ourselves from prematurely seeking zealous reforms before we stop to see what God may be doing with institutions and authorities that appear unworthy to us.

When you understand what God is doing through His left hand Kingdom (preserving a society that furthers the spread of the gospel), you can understand how He can even use sinful, unbelieving people to promote peace and temporal justice. Think of all the people right now who are doing a “good” job in their vocations as politicians, police, entrepreneurs, business people, and even fathers and mothers, even though they aren’t Christian. They know, however, that they need to do the right thing for others in their work. Is that optimal? No. But God works through that to keep a neighborhood, a community, and even a nation from imploding.

body.quote: My Kingdom is not of this world.

body: Martin Luther captured the essence of this Two-kingdom teaching in his writings. Christians need to remember Christ’s words to Pilate in John 18:36 and restrain themselves from trying to legislate God’s Kingdom into existence here on earth. So, most of the time, we Christians let the rulers rule, enjoying the temporal peace and security God brings us through them, and not demanding a theocracy built around our own utopian vision.

Nevertheless, our Christian respect for those in authority is not absolute. As Acts 5:29 teaches, “we must obey God rather than men.” Romans 13 teaches that the government is to be a terror to evil doers and an encouragement to those who do good, and when the government oversteps its God-given left-hand kingdom role and begins to persecute the church for speaking the truth about good and evil (like it is even here in America with those who speak out against abortion and gay marriage) we can and must speak out all the more. Even so, it is not with a rebellious heart that we resist evil government, but a loving heart that earnestly “desires all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” (1 Timothy 2:4)

Reformation Restraint is the belief that God is at work in the world, even through unbelievers, and that he has a plan to achieve the best for every person. Jesus himself tells us that “all authority in heaven and on earth” has been given to Him. Restraint, therefore, is recognition that God has instituted government, and even if living Christian life demands resistance to that government, God’s people still eagerly wait to see his plan. Reformation restraint means counting on him, even when we’re tempted to take matters into our own hands.
questions: What does it mean to you to practice restraint when it comes to left-hand kingdom involvement?
What is the advantage of practicing restraint when it comes to responding to political, cultural, and social issues?
Why does the Christian practice restraint when it comes to open rebellion against a law?
